statement: Let $\\omega=\\cos\\frac{2\\pi}{5}+i\\sin\\frac{2\\pi}{5}$, a primitive fifth root of unity. (i) Show that $1+\\omega+\\omega^{2}+\\omega^{3}+\\omega^{4}=0$. (ii) Show that $\\omega\\omega^{2}\\omega^{3}\\omega^{4}=1$. (iii) Deduce that $\\cos\\frac{2\\pi}{5}+\\cos\\frac{4\\pi}{5}=-\\frac{1}{2}$.
solution: (i) $\\omega$ satisfies $\\omega^{5}=1$ and $\\omega\\neq 1$, so $(\\omega^{5}-1)/(\\omega-1)=1+\\omega+\\dots+\\omega^{4}=0$. (ii) Product $=\\omega^{1+2+3+4}=\\omega^{10}=(\\omega^{5})^{2}=1$. (iii) Taking real parts of (i): $1+2\\cos(2\\pi/5)+2\\cos(4\\pi/5)=0$, so $\\cos(2\\pi/5)+\\cos(4\\pi/5)=-1/2$.
hints: Add the conjugates to extract cosines.
